headline: Red Sox escape Baltimore with a win and zero heart attacks
morning_brew: That was a damn relief. Ranger Suarez was dealing on the mound, keeping Baltimore quiet for seven full innings while Mickey Gasper provided all the firepower we needed with that first-inning blast. It wasn't pretty, and the eighth-inning fireworks made me nervous as hell, but we walked out of Camden Yards with a 1-0 win. My mother watched the whole thing and said it felt like we were playing in a phone booth, and she is not wrong; it was tighter than the parking situation at Fenway on a bobblehead night.

Benches clearing in the eighth after a hard slide by Blaze Alexander turned a quiet night into a full-blown argument, but the boys didn't let it get under their skin. I love that kind of grit, even if it does make the game last an hour longer than it needs to. We have been needing a night where the pitching actually holds serve, and Suarez, Whitlock, and Chapman were lights out. It is about damn time we saw that kind of command.

We are sitting at 77-65 and still fighting for every scrap of ground in the Wild Card race. I am not saying we are out of the woods, but seeing them close out a one-run game without the arson squad making an appearance is a massive step forward. Let us bring that same intensity to the yard for the rest of this weekend series.

news_digest.headline: Benches clear in Red Sox-Orioles after Blaze Alexander's hard slide
news_digest.dans_take: It is September baseball, tempers are gonna flare, but as long as we put a W on the board, I don't care.
